Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LOT 3531-3, LC-USZ62-61418, LC-DIG-stereo-1s42977 (item 2005694911).
author: C. H. Graves (publisher)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 1s42977u.tif (5860 x 3010), read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The left-hand frame: a maid seen from behind at a kitchen range, full length at about three metres, her mistress facing the camera beyond her.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Used only as a reference picture the 1904 house maid is judged against and for the back of her apron (T-3448); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3448) from the master TIFF. The maid, seen from behind, wears a light shirtwaist (sooty handprints on its back are part of the joke), a dark gored skirt to the floor and a checked apron whose ties are knotted in a bow at the back of the waist; her hair is drawn up. Her mistress wears a wide trimmed hat and a high-collared white shirtwaist. A staged comic scene, not Chicago and not of any named servant; the date (c1905) is the catalogue's, which marks its caption-card data 'unverified, old data'; the publisher is read from the mount, lettered 'The Art Nouveau (Platino) Stereograph, C. H. Graves, Publisher, Phila., U.S.A.', which the catalogue does not name.
note: One of the 1904 house maid reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/maid_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: the back of a maid's working dress: the apron ties' bow at the waist and the skirt falling to the floor
that a print or checked apron and a light shirtwaist were also worn for rough work
